definition: Existing as an idea or feeling rather than as something you can touch.
example: Freedom is an abstract idea, not an object you can hold.

options.text: Like an idea you cannot touch
Like a rock you can pick up
Like a tool you can hold in your hand
Like a book you can read

explanation: Abstract describes an idea that you cannot touch. Nice work!

definition: To change in order to fit a new situation or place.
example: Some plants adapt to dry weather by storing water in their stems.

options.text: To stay the same in every place
To change to fit a new situation
To leave a place and not return
To ask for help with a task

explanation: To adapt is to change to fit a new situation. Great job!

definition: To study something closely, part by part, to understand it.
example: In science class, we analyze the data from our experiment.

options.text: To hurry through something quickly
To study something part by part
To copy something onto a clean page
To forget something you just learned

explanation: To analyze is to study something part by part. You got it!

definition: To expect something and get ready for it.
example: We anticipate a big crowd at the fair, so we are bringing extra chairs.

options.text: To expect something and get ready
To forget something and leave it behind
To remember something from long ago
To ignore something and walk away

explanation: To anticipate is to expect something and get ready. Well done!

definition: To value something and feel thankful for it.
example: I appreciate your help with the heavy boxes.

options.text: To ignore something given to you
To complain about something small
To forget who gave you something
To value something and be thankful

explanation: To appreciate is to value something and be thankful. Nice work!

definition: One part or side of something that you can look at.
example: The cost is one aspect of the plan, but safety matters too.

options.text: The whole of a thing from end to end
The reason behind a final decision
One side of a bigger idea
The ending of a long, twisting story

explanation: An aspect is one side or part of a bigger idea. Great job!

definition: A good result or advantage that you get from something.
example: One benefit of exercise is that it gives you more energy.

options.text: A good result you get from something
A bad habit that is very hard to break
A cost you must pay for something
A rule that limits what you can do

explanation: A benefit is a good result you get from something. You got it!

definition: To move around freely, passing from place to place.
example: A fan helps air circulate around the room.

options.text: To stay stuck in one spot
To drop quickly toward the ground
To grow smaller bit by bit
To move around and keep flowing

explanation: To circulate is to move around and keep flowing. Well done!

definition: Made of many parts and hard to understand.
example: The rules of the board game were so complex that it took us an hour to learn them.

options.text: Having many connected parts
Having only one simple part
Having parts that are all the same
Having one part that is hidden

explanation: Complex means having many connected parts. Nice work!

definition: One part of a larger whole, such as a part of a machine.
example: The battery is a key component of the flashlight.

options.text: The whole of a finished object
The box that an object comes in
The manual that explains an object
One part of a larger whole

explanation: A component is one part of a larger whole. Great job!

definition: A result of something that happened earlier.
example: One consequence of staying up late is feeling sleepy in class.

options.text: A reason for doing something later
A result of something done earlier
A prize given to the best player
A warning printed on a sign

explanation: A consequence is a result of something done earlier. You got it!

definition: Always acting or happening in the same way.
example: She is a consistent player who practices every single day.

options.text: Changing in a new way each and every time
Happening only once in a while
Always happening in the same way
Happening at the wrong time

explanation: Consistent means always happening in the same way. Well done!

definition: The words or situation around something that help explain its meaning.
example: You can figure out a new word by reading the context around it.

options.text: The very last page of a long, thick story book
The title at the top of a page
The surrounding words that give meaning
The list of words at the back

explanation: Context is the surrounding words that give meaning. Nice work!

definition: To reach a conclusion by thinking about clues.
example: From the wet umbrella, I deduce that it rained today.

options.text: To work out an answer from clues
To hide the clues from other people
To ignore the clues and guess
To tell the clues to a friend

explanation: To deduce is to work out an answer from clues. Great job!

definition: A hard choice between two or more things.
example: She faced a dilemma: join the soccer team or the art club.

options.text: An easy task that takes only a minute
A hard choice between two options
A plan that works every time
A story that has no ending

explanation: A dilemma is a hard choice between two options. You got it!

definition: Made up of many different kinds.
example: The park has a diverse mix of trees, from tall pines to small maples.

options.text: Made up of only one kind
Made up of parts that match exactly
Made up of many different kinds
Made up of things in a straight line

explanation: Diverse means made up of many different kinds. Well done!

definition: The way a place makes, shares and spends money, goods and services.
example: The town's economy grew when new shops opened.

options.text: How a place looks from the sky
How a place makes and uses money
How a place keeps its weather records
How a place names its streets

explanation: An economy is how a place makes and uses money. Nice work!

definition: To add more details to explain something.
example: Can you elaborate on how you built the model?

options.text: To remove details to make it shorter
To add more details to explain
To repeat the same sentence again
To change the topic suddenly

explanation: To elaborate is to add more details to explain. Great job!

definition: To remove or get rid of something completely.
example: Chefs try to eliminate waste by using every part of a vegetable.

options.text: To remove something completely
To add something more
To hide something for later
To count something twice

explanation: To eliminate is to remove something completely. You got it!

definition: To give special importance to something so that it stands out.
example: The teacher will emphasize the main idea by underlining it.

options.text: To make something blend into the background
To tell something quietly to no one
To show that something is important
To skip over something very quickly

explanation: To emphasize is to show that something is important. Well done!

definition: To judge how good or useful something is after careful thought.
example: The judges will evaluate each science project.

options.text: To judge how good something is
To build something from scratch
To ignore something without a thought
To guess without looking at it

explanation: To evaluate is to judge how good something is. Nice work!

definition: Having more than one possible meaning, so it is unclear.
example: The sign was ambiguous, so we could not tell which way to turn.

options.text: Having more than one meaning
Having only one clear meaning
Having been said more than once
Having no words in it at all

explanation: Ambiguous means having more than one possible meaning. Great job!

definition: To make something sound bigger or better than it really is.
example: I exaggerate when I say that the walk took forever.

options.text: To make something sound smaller than it is
To make something sound bigger than it is
To tell something just as it happened
To say something in a very quiet voice

explanation: To exaggerate is to make something sound bigger than it is. You got it!

definition: To rise and fall again and again.
example: The temperature can fluctuate a lot during a spring day.

options.text: To climb steadily without stopping
To stay frozen at one level
To fall once and then stop
To rise and fall again and again

explanation: To fluctuate is to rise and fall again and again. Well done!

definition: An idea that you can test to explain why something happens.
example: Our hypothesis was that plants grow taller with more light.

options.text: A fact that is already proved
A tool for measuring plants
A list of the steps in a game
An idea that you can test

explanation: A hypothesis is an idea that you can test. Nice work!

definition: To explain or show something with pictures or examples.
example: The author used a diagram to illustrate how a lever works.

options.text: To cover something up with paint
To explain with pictures or examples
To read about something aloud
To copy something word for word

explanation: To illustrate is to explain with pictures or examples. Great job!

definition: The power to change what people think or do.
example: A good teacher can have a lasting influence on students.

options.text: The strength to lift something heavy
The speed at which something moves
The size of a crowd at an event
The power to affect what people do

explanation: Influence is the power to affect what people think or do. You got it!

definition: To explain the meaning of something.
example: Can you interpret what the poem is saying?

options.text: To explain what something means
To hide what something means
To copy what something looks like
To forget what something said

explanation: To interpret is to explain what something means. Well done!

definition: To set something apart so that it is alone.
example: We will isolate one plant in a dark closet to see if it still grows.

options.text: To join something to a larger group
To put something in the center of a crowd
To pass something to many people
To set something apart from the rest

explanation: To isolate is to set something apart from the rest. Nice work!

definition: To give good reasons to show that something is fair or right.
example: Please justify your answer by showing your work.

options.text: To change a choice at the last minute
To hide a choice from other people
To give good reasons for a choice
To make a choice by flipping a coin

explanation: To justify is to give good reasons for a choice. Great job!

definition: To keep something in good shape or going at the same level.
example: We maintain our bikes by oiling the chains.

options.text: To let something fall apart
To keep something in good shape
To trade something for a new one
To sell something at a low price

explanation: To maintain is to keep something in good shape. You got it!

definition: The parts of a machine that work together to do a job.
example: The clock's mechanism is made of tiny gears.

options.text: The case that covers a machine
The cord that plugs a machine into the wall
The label stuck onto a machine
The parts that work together in a machine

explanation: A mechanism is the working parts of a machine. Well done!

definition: To talk with others to reach an agreement.
example: The two teams will negotiate to decide who gets the field first.

options.text: To wait quietly for others to decide
To follow the rules without a word
To talk to reach an agreement
To ask a question and walk away

explanation: To negotiate is to talk to reach an agreement. Nice work!

definition: Not taking either side in a disagreement.
example: The referee stays neutral and treats both teams the same.

options.text: Siding with the stronger team
Not taking either side
Cheering only for the home team
Leaving before the game starts

explanation: Neutral means not taking either side. Great job!

definition: A way of looking at something, based on your own point of view.
example: From my perspective, the hike was fun, but my sister found it long.

options.text: A way of looking at something
A map that shows a short route
A tool used for seeing far away
A rule that says who goes first

explanation: A perspective is a way of looking at something. You got it!

definition: Something that can be seen or noticed, especially in nature.
example: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon caused by sunlight and water drops.

options.text: A tool used to measure the daily weather
A rule that explains how to play
A place where scientists work
An event in nature that can be seen

explanation: A phenomenon is something in nature that can be seen. Well done!

definition: Seeming reasonable and likely to be true.
example: The idea that the wind blew the door shut seemed plausible.

options.text: Seeming reasonable and likely true
Certainly false and easy to prove wrong
Meant only to make people laugh
Too hard for anyone to follow

explanation: Plausible means seeming reasonable and likely true. Nice work!

definition: Something that is more important than other things and should come first.
example: Finishing my homework is my priority before I play.

options.text: Something that can wait until later
Something that is left over from yesterday
Something that should be done first
Something that is shared by everyone

explanation: A priority is something that should be done first. Great job!

definition: The size of one part compared with another part or the whole.
example: The proportion of blue beads to red beads is two to one.

options.text: The place where something is kept
The name given to a new idea
The speed of a moving object
The size of a part compared to a whole

explanation: A proportion compares the size of a part to a whole. You got it!

definition: Not eager to do something.
example: He was reluctant to try the diving board at first.

options.text: Too excited to wait a second
Able to finish very quickly
Not eager to do something
Ready to try anything new

explanation: Reluctant means not eager to do something. Well done!

definition: Important and worth noticing.
example: Finding the fossil was a significant moment for the whole class.

options.text: Small and very easy to overlook
Plain and not at all unusual
Old and no longer used
Important and worth noticing

explanation: Significant means important and worth noticing. Nice work!

definition: To keep something going for a long time.
example: A strong root system helps sustain the tree through dry summers.

options.text: To stop something right away
To start something brand new
To keep something going for a long time
To change something into a new shape

explanation: To sustain is to keep something going for a long time. Great job!

definition: An idea, backed by evidence, that explains how or why something works.
example: The theory explains why the tides rise and fall each day.

options.text: A tool scientists use to see tiny things
A rule that people must obey
A prize given at a science fair
An idea that explains how something works

explanation: A theory is an idea that explains how something works. You got it!

definition: Clear enough to see through, like clean glass.
example: The transparent bottle let us see the water level.

options.text: Thick enough that light cannot pass
Dark enough to hide what is inside
Clear enough that you can see through
Solid enough to stand on

explanation: Transparent means clear enough to see through. Well done!

definition: Final, or the greatest of its kind.
example: Reaching the top of the hill was the ultimate goal of our hike.

options.text: First and smallest of its kind
Final or greatest of its kind
Oldest and most worn of the group
Most average of all in the group

explanation: Ultimate means final or the greatest of its kind. Nice work!

definition: One of a kind, unlike anything else.
example: Every snowflake has a unique shape.

options.text: One of many that look the same
One of two that go together
One of a kind, unlike any other
One of a crowd that is easy to miss

explanation: Unique means one of a kind. Great job!

definition: To check that something is true or correct.
example: Use a second book to verify the facts in your report.

options.text: To wish that something were true
To pretend that something is true
To copy something that is true
To check that something is true

explanation: To verify is to check that something is true. You got it!

definition: Bright, clear and full of life or detail.
example: Her vivid painting showed every color of the sunset.

options.text: Dull and hard to make out
Bright and full of life
Plain and a little faded
Loud and harsh to hear

explanation: Vivid means bright and full of life. Well done!

definition: To say or show the opposite of what was said before.
example: Your two answers contradict each other, so one of them must be wrong.

options.text: To say the opposite of what was said
To say the very same thing again
To say nothing at all in reply
To say something in a rush

explanation: To contradict is to say the opposite of what was said. Nice work!

definition: Closely connected to the topic you are talking about.
example: Only include facts that are relevant to your topic.

options.text: Not connected to the topic at all
Closely connected to the topic
Placed at the top of a long list
Listed in alphabetical order

explanation: Relevant means closely connected to the topic. Great job!
